svg.title: Endothelial cells in cardiac fibrosis
svg.desc: A 16:9 vector evidence synthesis of 41 endothelial findings in 26 source entries, drawn from both sheets of the supplied workbook. Three panels show endothelial states, metabolic and cellular signaling, and vascular remodeling with preclinical repair approaches. Numbered circles link to the papers and contain citation tooltips.

svg.text: Vascular identity, metabolic plasticity and multicellular control of injury and repair

g.title:
Healthy human cardiac endothelium includes capillary, arterial, venous, lymphatic and endocardial states. Rare mixed transcriptional features do not establish lineage conversion.
CF011-EC-F01: Resolved 10 vascular/mesothelial clusters: capillary ECs (EC1–3), immune ECs (EC4), arterial ECs (EC5; SEMA3G+), venous ECs (EC6; ACKR1+), atrial ECs (EC7), lymphatic ECs (EC8; PROX1+), and rare ECs with FB/CM features Evidence as supplied: Observational

a.aria-label: Reference 22: Litviňuková M et al. 2020. Cells of the adult human heart
a.title: [22] Litviňuková M et al. (2020). Cells of the adult human heart. Nature. DOI: 10.1038/s41586-020-2797-4

g.title:
MI and TAC trajectories are shown separately. Early MI abundance shifts are relative single-cell fractions. Transient mesenchymal activation and glycolytic shifts can resolve; cycling and reparative ECs after TAC rise at two weeks and decline by four weeks.
CF063-EC-F01: Post-MI ECs populating Monocle State 4 (characterized by Col3a1, Fn1, Serpine1 enrichment and Cdh5 downregulation) peaked at d3–d5 (81%–65%) and returned to baseline by d14 (14%) Evidence as supplied: Observational
CF063-EC-F02: GFP+ cells expressed mesenchymal transcripts (Col1a1, Serpine1, Col3a1) at d3–d7, but remained non-fibroblast clusters and returned to endothelial baseline clusters by d14–d28 Evidence as supplied: Lineage tracing
CF063-EC-F03: EndMA+ ECs displayed upregulated glycolytic genes (Ldha, Eno1, Pfkp) and downregulated fatty acid oxidation genes (Fabp4); TGF-β2-induced mesenchymal markers (TAGLN, CNN1) fully reversed 7d post-withdrawal Evidence as supplied: Functional perturbation
CF060-EC-F01: Cycling ECs (CyclEC) and Reparative/Angiogenic ECs (RepEC marked by Apln) expanded at 2w post-TAC but significantly declined below baseline by 4w; Endocardial (EndoEC) and Lymphatic (LymEC) proportions decreased Evidence as supplied: Lineage tracing
1-s2.0-S2211124720301625-main-F01: Identified distinct endothelial (Fabp4, Pecam1) and lymphatic endothelial (Lyve1, Cldn5) clusters; EC relative abundance dropped markedly during early inflammatory influx (d1–d3) and recovered during proliferative/maturation phases (d5–d28) Evidence as supplied: Observational
CF029-EC-F01: Interstitial non-myocyte sequencing captured major EC sub-populations alongside shifting stromal and leukocyte pools during post-MI inflammatory (d3) and proliferative (d7) phases Evidence as supplied: Observational

g.text: MI d1–3: relative EC abundance falls
TAC Cycling / APLN+ reparative ECs ↑ at 2 wk, ↓ at 4 wk

g.title:
Human disease observations: acute ischemic capillary loss and spatial stress niches; lymphatic/angiogenic EC expansion in chronic ICM; arterial EC fraction and global expression shifts in DCM; genotype/chamber-specific EC state composition and endocardial BMP6 in DSP hearts. Changes in fractions are not absolute vessel counts.
CF004-EC-F01: ICM LV myocardium displayed significant increases in EC-lymphatic (CCL21+, logFC=5.2) clustered in fibrotic zones and EC-angiogenic (MYO1B+, logFC=2.15) localized in microvascular capillaries Evidence as supplied: Observational
10.1038/s41586-022-05060-x-F01: Identified 5 EC subtypes (capillary, arterial, venous, lymphatic, endocardial). Capillary ECs were depleted in acute ischemic zones, while molecular niche 10 (enriched in capillary ECs, pericytes, and mast cells) showed elevated hypoxia and TGF-β signaling Evidence as supplied: Observational
CF006-EC-F01: Identified distinct arterial (Ec3), venous (Ec2), capillary (Ec1), lymphatic (Ec4), and endocardial (Ecd1/Ecd2) clusters. DCM hearts exhibited a significant increase in arterial ECs (Ec3) and global transcriptomic shifts rather than sub-state diversification Evidence as supplied: Observational
CF008-EC-F01: Identified 7 EC states (EC1–8); DCM LVs showed a significant increase in EC5 and altered EC1:EC2/EC5/EC6 ratios. Endocardial BMP6 was markedly upregulated in DSP mutant hearts; no changes in EMT or EC apoptosis scores were detected Evidence as supplied: Observational

g.text: Capillary ECs depleted; hypoxia / TGF-β niches.
CCL21+ lymphatic and MYO1B+ angiogenic ECs ↑.
Arterial EC fraction ↑; broad transcriptional shifts.
Chamber-specific EC ratios; endocardial BMP6 ↑ in DSP.

g.title:
Inducible MI and TAC lineage experiments support transient mesenchymal activation or endothelial lineage stability in the studied models. Marker co-expression in the metabolic studies does not prove permanent conversion to fibroblasts.
zhang-et-al-2021-F01: 99.4%–99.5% of tdT+ lineage-traced ECs maintained CD31/CDH5 expression at 7d and 28d post-TAC; 0% expressed α-SMA or PDGFRA Evidence as supplied: Lineage tracing
CF060-EC-F02: Each fate-traced lineage retained its distinct transcriptomic boundaries post-TAC; no tdTom+ ECs converted to fibroblasts and no stromal lineages converted to endothelium Evidence as supplied: Lineage tracing

g.data-finding-ids: CF058-EC-F01 CF058-EC-F02 CF058-EC-F03 CF058-EC-F04 CF058-EC-F05 CF061-EC-F01 CF061-EC-F02 CF061-EC-F03
g.title:
Two study-specific metabolic mechanisms induce mesenchymal markers and function. Lactate entry promotes CBP/p300-associated Snail1 lactylation and TGFB1/SMAD2 signaling. PFKFB3 drives glycolysis at the expense of PPP-derived NADPH, with mitochondrial Fe–S and respiratory impairment. Marker changes are not represented as a definitive lineage conversion.
CF058-EC-F01: Supplemental lactate reduced endothelial markers (Cdh5, Kdr) and increased mesenchymal markers (Col1a1, Fn1, S100a4, α-SMA, FSP1) Evidence as supplied: Functional perturbation
CF058-EC-F02: Lactate treatment increased GFP+FSP1+ co-localization and elevated GFP+gp38+ cell proportion in post-MI myocardium Evidence as supplied: Lineage tracing
CF058-EC-F03: Hypoxia plus lactate accelerated Snail1 nuclear translocation and significantly increased Snail1 recruitment to the TGFB1 promoter Evidence as supplied: Functional perturbation
CF058-EC-F04: Lactate promoted Snail1 interaction with CBP/p300 and increased Snail1 lysine lactylation (Kla); CHC blocked Snail1 lactylation and CBP/p300 association Evidence as supplied: Functional perturbation
CF058-EC-F05: Snail1 knock-down restored CD31/VE-cadherin levels, reduced α-SMA/FSP1/COL1A1, suppressed p-SMAD2, and rescued post-MI LVEF% and FS% Evidence as supplied: Functional perturbation
CF061-EC-F01: TGF-β1 reduced CD31 and increased α-SMA, PFKFB3, and gel contraction; SAC dose-dependently restored CD31, suppressed α-SMA/PFKFB3, and inhibited gel contraction Evidence as supplied: Functional perturbation
CF061-EC-F02: Forcing OxPhos (DCA/galactose) or pharmacological PFKFB3 inhibition reduced lactate and blocked EndoMT; PFKFB3 overexpression blunted SAC protection and impaired mitochondrial Fe-S clusters (ACO2, NDUFS1) Evidence as supplied: Functional perturbation
CF061-EC-F03: Endothelial Pfkfb3 overexpression exacerbated TAC-induced perivascular fibrosis and CD31+α-SMA+ co-localization; endothelial Pfkfb3 silencing reduced fibrosis and restored cardiac function Evidence as supplied: Functional perturbation

g.title:
Cardiomyocyte ZEB2 induces TMSB4/PTMA-mediated endothelial migration, sprouting and proliferation in conditioned-medium studies. Cardiomyocyte-specific Zeb2 overexpression improves vascularization, scar and function in mouse MI.
CF071-EC-F01: CM-CM from ZEB2-overexpressing CMs significantly increased HUVEC migration, sprout number, cumulative sprout length, and EdU+ proliferation; ZEB2 knock-down in CMs reduced sprouting and proliferation Evidence as supplied: Functional perturbation (Sender-Receiver)
CF071-EC-F02: Zeb2 cTg mice exhibited significantly elevated border/remote zone PECAM1+ capillary vessel area, decreased Sirius Red scar area, and improved fractional shortening (FS%) post-MI Evidence as supplied: Functional perturbation

a.title: [5] Gladka MM et al. (2021). Cardiomyocytes stimulate angiogenesis after ischemic injury in a ZEB2-dependent manner. Nature Communications. DOI: 10.1038/s41467-020-20361-3

g.text: ZEB2 → TMSB4 / PTMA → migration, sprouting, proliferation.
Mouse MI: capillaries ↑, scar ↓, cardiac function ↑.

g.title:
Mouse post-MI IL-1β/TGF-β2/IFN-γ signaling induces transient MHC-II-positive immunomodulatory ECs and T-cell interactions. Human fibrotic HF contains DARC/CCL14/SELE/VCAM1-positive activated ECs associated with inflammatory macrophages; recruitment is a proposed consequence, not proven by expression alone.
CF057-EC-F01: Identified a transient hybrid EC subset (Immunomodulatory ECs, IMECs; Id1+Mgll+ arterial / Plvap+vWF+ venous origin) expressing MHC-II and hematopoietic/immune genes, peaking at d1 post-MI in the infarct border zone Evidence as supplied: Observational
CF057-EC-F02: Cytokine cocktail cooperatively induced the IMEC signature in vitro; EC-specific deletion of IFN-γ signaling reduced T-cell activation and significantly improved post-MI cardiac healing Evidence as supplied: Functional perturbation
s00395-021-00897-1-F01: Activated EC subset (enriched in severely fibrotic DCM LV and ICM MI) specifically expressed DARC (Duffy antigen), CCL14, SELE, VCAM1, and transcription factors NR2F2 / CEBPD; interacted with CXCL8hiCCR2+HLA-DRhi macrophages Evidence as supplied: Observational

g.text: IL-1β / TGF-β2 / IFN-γ → MHC-II+ IMECs (MI d1–3).
IMECs interact with and activate T cells in mouse MI.
Human HF: DARC / CCL14 / SELE / VCAM1+ ECs

g.title:
Computationally inferred EC laminin–integrin signaling targets cardiomyocytes, fibroblasts and pericytes in human ICM. Connectome analysis links ECs with activated fibroblasts under AngII stress. Perivascular PI16/DPP4 fibroblast niches and arterial/SMC–fibroblast spatial coupling are observed or modeled; spatial association is not a causal interaction.
CF004-EC-F02: Inferred a striking increase in LAMININ pathway signaling from ECs (via ligands LAMA4, LAMB1, LAMC1) targeting integrin receptors (ITGA1, ITGA3, ITGAV, ITGB1) on cardiomyocytes, fibroblasts, and pericytes Evidence as supplied: Computational prediction (Sender: EC)
CF001-EC-F01: Juxta-view spatial modeling revealed that perivascular arterial ECs (EC_art) and SMCs tightly co-localized with specific perivascular fibroblast sub-states (FB2) in NF hearts, whereas SMC-to-FB3 spatial dependency was lost in MI-fibrotic scar tissue (p<0.05) Evidence as supplied: Computational prediction (Sender: EC_art/SMC)
CF002-EC-F01: Discriminative stem/progenitor-like fibroblast subset (F-SH / Pi16high / Dpp4+) was localized specifically to the perivascular adventitia surrounding mid-to-small caliber coronary arteries Evidence as supplied: Observational
CF026-EC-F01: Subclustering revealed shifting EC sub-populations under AngII stress. Intercellular network analysis identified ECs as major receivers and paracrine signal senders of growth factors (Vegfa, Vegfc, Fgf2, Pfgfa/b) interacting with expanding Cilp+/Thbs4+ activated fibroblasts Evidence as supplied: Computational prediction (Sender: EC / Receiver: EC)
g.text: Predicted: EC laminins → integrins on CMs / FBs / pericytes.
Growth-factor networks link ECs and activated fibroblasts.
PI16+ / DPP4+ adventitial FBs surround coronary arteries.
Spatial vascular–FB coupling is altered in MI scar.

g.title:
Adding primitive human PSC-derived macrophages to engineered cardiac tissue increases MMP secretion, prevents vessel regression, and supports patent perfusable vessels, tissue viability and contractile performance for up to two weeks. This is an engineered-tissue experiment, not an in vivo fibrosis intervention.
nihms-2006234-F01: Adding primitive macrophages prevented short-term vessel regression, increased MMP secretion, and promoted long-term perfusable CD31+ microvessels with superior tissue viability and contractile performance Evidence as supplied: Functional perturbation (Sender: Macrophage)

g.text: Human engineered tissue: MMP secretion ↑; perfusability,
viability and contractile function ↑ (up to 2 wk).

g.title:
MI mural detachment is associated with capillary loss. Partial mural ablation causally disrupts CDH5 junctions, increases permeability and inflammatory adhesion molecules; pericyte transwell support increases CDH5 and reduces IL-6/ICAM1/VCAM1. Aging reduces coverage and RGS5. RGS5-deficient pericytes activate fibroblasts via TGF-β2 without increasing leakage or leukocyte infiltration.
CF074-EC-F01: 18-month-old hearts showed significantly reduced pericyte area and capillary coverage normalized to IB4+ area (p=0.008), accompanied by down-regulated Rgs5 UMI in pericytes (p=0.002) Evidence as supplied: Observational
CF074-EC-F02: Rgs5ΔPC mice developed pericyte branch widening, progressive EF% reduction (8w p=0.001), increased LV mass, and diffuse myocardial Sirius Red fibrosis without changing microvascular permeability or leukocyte infiltration; RGS5-deficient pericyte supernatant induced α-SMA in fibroblasts via TGF-β2 Evidence as supplied: Functional perturbation
CF059-EC-F01: Infarct zone exhibited rapid, persistent microvascular vessel loss by d5 PI with severe detachment/reduction of mural cell coverage around ECs; remote zone maintained pro-angiogenic signals while infarct zone sustained anti-angiogenic/inflammatory signals Evidence as supplied: Observational
CF076-EC-F01: Partial pericyte ablation reduced capillary density, induced discontinuous endothelial CADHERIN-5 (CDH5) junctions, elevated ICAM-1 and VCAM-1 expression, and significantly increased fibrinogen extravasation into the myocardium Evidence as supplied: Functional perturbation
CF076-EC-F02: Co-culture with pericytes significantly increased CDH5 protein in HMVEC-Cs (p=0.0175) and suppressed inflammatory transcripts (IL-6 p=0.0011, ICAM-1 p=0.0207, VCAM-1 p=0.0293) and ICAM-1 protein Evidence as supplied: Functional perturbation (Sender: Pericyte)

a.title: [13] Cornuault L et al. (2023). Partial mural cell ablation disrupts coronary vasculature integrity and induces cardiac dysfunction. Circulation Research. DOI: 10.1161/CIRCRESAHA.122.321876

g.text: Mural loss → CDH5 gaps, leakage, capillary loss,
Pericyte co-culture: CDH5 ↑; IL-6 / ICAM1 / VCAM1 ↓.
Aging / RGS5 loss → pericyte TGF-β2 → FB activation.
RGS5-loss fibrosis occurs without increased permeability.

g.title:
Review framework: early mural detachment and leak, macrophage VEGFA/VEGFC during sprouting, and PDGF-BB/PDGFRβ plus TGF-β/TGFBR2 during mural re-coverage. Pericyte fate tracing shows fibrogenic phenotypic modulation; pericyte-specific Tgfbr2 perturbation alters vascular maturation.
nihms-1906932-F01: Dual lineage tracing showed pericytes enwrap capillary ECs; post-MI pericytes detached from microvessels and acquired a fibroblast-like profile. Pericyte-specific Tgfbr2 deletion altered pericyte detachment and post-MI vascular stabilization Evidence as supplied: Lineage tracing
nihms-1993103-F01: Inflammatory phase pericytes detach from ECs causing hyperpermeability; proliferative phase efferocytosing macrophages secrete VEGFA/VEGFC; maturation phase pericytes re-coat microvessels via PDGF-BB/PDGFRβ and TGF-β/TGFBR2 Evidence as supplied: Background review
g.text: Repair depends on phase and mural signals

PDGFRβ and TGF-β / TGFBR2 guide mural maturation.

g.title:
Experimental interventions are not one combined regimen: MCT blockade in vitro and Snail1 silencing in cells/mouse MI; PFKFB3 suppression or SAC in cells and mouse TAC/ISO; endothelial IFNGR1 depletion initiated before mouse MI; MEK inhibitor-driven pericyte reprogramming and mouse post-MI vascularization; PDGF-AB improves pig post-MI vascularity. DCA/galactose or PFKFB3 inhibitors also support the metabolic mechanism in vitro.
CF058-EC-F04: Lactate promoted Snail1 interaction with CBP/p300 and increased Snail1 lysine lactylation (Kla); CHC blocked Snail1 lactylation and CBP/p300 association Evidence as supplied: Functional perturbation
CF058-EC-F05: Snail1 knock-down restored CD31/VE-cadherin levels, reduced α-SMA/FSP1/COL1A1, suppressed p-SMAD2, and rescued post-MI LVEF% and FS% Evidence as supplied: Functional perturbation
CF057-EC-F02: Cytokine cocktail cooperatively induced the IMEC signature in vitro; EC-specific deletion of IFN-γ signaling reduced T-cell activation and significantly improved post-MI cardiac healing Evidence as supplied: Functional perturbation
CF061-EC-F01: TGF-β1 reduced CD31 and increased α-SMA, PFKFB3, and gel contraction; SAC dose-dependently restored CD31, suppressed α-SMA/PFKFB3, and inhibited gel contraction Evidence as supplied: Functional perturbation
CF061-EC-F02: Forcing OxPhos (DCA/galactose) or pharmacological PFKFB3 inhibition reduced lactate and blocked EndoMT; PFKFB3 overexpression blunted SAC protection and impaired mitochondrial Fe-S clusters (ACO2, NDUFS1) Evidence as supplied: Functional perturbation
CF061-EC-F03: Endothelial Pfkfb3 overexpression exacerbated TAC-induced perivascular fibrosis and CD31+α-SMA+ co-localization; endothelial Pfkfb3 silencing reduced fibrosis and restored cardiac function Evidence as supplied: Functional perturbation
CF077-EC-F01: MEK inhibitor-treated pericytes acquired VSMC contractile proteins (α-SMA, SM-MHC), reduced ANGPT-2 secretion, and significantly enhanced CAEC tube network length when co-cultured in Matrigel (p<0.01) Evidence as supplied: Functional perturbation
CF077-EC-F02: Short-term oral PD0325901 treatment post-MI significantly increased peri-infarct α-SMA+ arteriole density and total vascular area, reduced scar size, and improved LV systolic function Evidence as supplied: Functional perturbation
scitranslmed.aay2140-F01: rhPDGF-AB significantly increased peri-infarct vWF+ capillary density (107 vs 56/mm2, p=0.001) and 3D light sheet arteriolar branching (220 vs 23 junctions/field, p=0.03) and arteriole counts (1919 vs 500/field, p=0.03) Evidence as supplied: Functional perturbation
g.text: MCT: cells; Snail1: cells / mouse MI (function ↑).

svg.text: Endothelial state, immune signaling and mural support connect cardiac injury to fibrosis and repair.
Sources: both workbook sheets; 41 findings from 26 linked entries. Eight additional indexed entries contain no extracted finding.
Evidence: human observations, cell / animal perturbations, fate mapping and computational predictions. Dashed arrows indicate predicted signaling.
Source status: AI-extracted; awaiting full paper review. Targeted checks applied. EC: endothelial cell; FB: fibroblast; MI: infarction; ICM / DCM: ischemic / dilated cardiomyopathy.
